<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines standard source entries: README and LICENSE files fetched via HTTPS from the project's GitHub repository, and a prebuilt binary tarball for x86_64. The URLs are constructed using variables that point to the legitimate upstream (https://github.com/programmersd21/nag), which aligns with expected packaging practices. The `sha256sums` and `sha256sums_x86_64` arrays contain valid checksums, indicating verification of the downloaded assets.

There is no command substitution, `pkgver()` function, or top-level code execution outside of variable assignment. The variables are statically defined or derived from `_gitversion`, which itself is set from `pkgver`. No dynamic fetching, evaluation, or execution occurs when sourcing the PKGBUILD. The use of `source_x86_64` and conditional checksums are standard in multi-architecture AUR packages.

Thus, running `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo` will safely fetch and verify sources without executing any malicious code.
</details>

</summary>

This does not constitute a supply-chain attack as there is no dynamic fetching, obfuscation, or unauthorized network activity.
